faqs.q: Do I really need Cyrillic keywords?
faqs.a: Yes. Most Bulgarian local searches happen in Cyrillic, and Google Bulgaria ranks Cyrillic pages for them. Latin transliteration covers a slice of younger mobile users and works as a secondary layer, but a transliteration-only strategy misses most of the market.

faqs.q: How long does SEO take in Bulgaria?
faqs.a: Faster than in most of Europe: early movement in 6 to 10 weeks, solid results in 3 to 5 months. Proper Bulgarian-language SEO is rare, so focused work moves quickly. The exception is Sofia's IT sector, where English B2B keywords compete globally.

faqs.q: Should coastal businesses target multiple languages?
faqs.a: Yes. The Black Sea coast draws Bulgarians, Romanians, and Western tourists, each searching in their own language. Covering the right languages multiplies your customer streams while monolingual competitors fight over one.

faqs.q: How important are reviews in Bulgaria?
faqs.a: Very important. Bulgarian buyers are careful and price-aware, and they rely on peer proof. Dozens of genuine Bulgarian reviews will out-convert a better-optimised site with none, and most competitors never systematise reviews.

faqs.q: Will I work with you directly?
faqs.a: Yes. I run a one-person studio, so the person researching your Cyrillic keywords is the person building your pages and writing your reports. Direct, no handoffs.
